title: India after the peak of parallel cinema; who has come closest in the 2000s to the kind of committed and sustained career of Ghatak, Ray, Sen etc

commenti.body:
Bengalí cinema was really bad this last 20 years. Aparna Sen is the only filmmaker I can think of.
Tamil on other hand is really in his prime Vetrimaaran. Pa ranjith, Mani ratnam, Menon, Bala, Ram, Subbaraj.... Great auteurs with a political commitment

It's true that there has been a tremendous drop-off in Bengali cinema since the glory days (which is partly why I created the thread). You mentioned Aparna Sen which made me also think of Konkona Sen Sharma who has worked with her and who may be of some interest to people here as well.

I agree that there has been an uptick in activity of note in Tamil film.

I would be interested in answers too!

The convincing heirs of this cinema, from the very little I've tried, seem to to be found earlier, in the 70s and 90s: Mani Kaul, Adoor Gopalakrishnan... Kumar Shahani, also, even if I didn't like the Bresson-like movie I've seen from him. It's not necessarily neorealist like the three filmmakers you mention, but I would definitely call that "parallel cinema". 

But for 2000-2020? No Idea. Apart from the mild-auteurish films which seem marketed for european arthouse audiences (*The Lunchbox*, Mira Nair...), or the more personal voices inside a frame which seem be the Hollywood one (Rituparno Ghosh) but that I would have difficulties to call "indie" (maybe I'm wrong on this?), I have no idea.

Not Indian, but if Satyajit Ray had an aesthetic heir it might have been the Abbas Kiarostami of *The Traveler* and *Where Is My Friend's House*? 

But you're talking about one of the greatest filmmakers of all time (and an author, and a musician, and a graphic designer -- a true Renaissance man) who leaves gigantic shoes for any heir to fill.

Well, Ray was far from a lone wolf in Bengali cinema and some (like myself) actually prefer Ghatak and Sen for example.

But yes, there has been plenty of discussion of the impact of Italian neorealism and Bengali cinema on Kiarostami and Iranian cinema more generally.

This thread though is about the heirs of that parallel cinema tradition in present day India.
